reasons.A: Short sentences fit, but it slips into second-person imperatives ('Wear long sleeves') and ends on generalising morals ('Some things are worth doing the slow way'), which the author's plain first-person account never does.
reasons.B: Closest movement and stance: steady first-person present, short declaratives with the author's own openings, flat assertion with no hedging, and a quiet concrete close in place of a moral.
reasons.C: Long subordinated sentences, a colon-led explanation and a how-to register ('the main risk') are far from the author's clipped, plain rhythm.
reasons.D: Right clipped first-person rhythm, but the verbless fragments and small dramatic notes ('This part takes nerve', 'Not a simmer.') plus explanations of why steps matter give it a slightly more instructional, performed voice than the author's.
